correctness.rationale: For every SPD A with eigenvalues in [mu,L], spectral-midpoint decomposition gives ||SAb|| >= (L+mu)||Sb||/2 -(L-mu)/2, hence sharp necessity. The explicit involution exchanges b and normalized Pb and has spectrum {-1,0,1}; thus A_eta is SPD with two exact extreme eigenvalues and sampled image eta Sb. Minimizing the resulting scalar squared residual yields the displayed exact ratio and shows divergence. The proof covers all n>s>=1 and all q>1, eta>0. check.py passed 62206 numerical assertions as supplementary reproducibility.

value.rationale: The dimension-sharp threshold answers a concrete numerical design gap between preserving the Krylov basis and preserving its matrix image in deterministic sketched GMRES. It shows that globally optimal coordinate preservation and even substantial fixed oversampling cannot safeguard true residual minimization, with arbitrarily well-conditioned SPD matrices when s/n tends to zero; and quantifies exactly the full residual divergence. This is a motivated algorithmic boundary, not a gratuitous small example or unmotivated parameter choice.
